title: Knowledge & RAG
markdown:
Retrieval is handled by `openexecutive.knowledge.retriever.retrieve`, querying ChromaDB collections through `openexecutive.knowledge.store.ChromaDBStore`. Five collections back the system:

- **BUILTIN** — curated MBA-style domain knowledge shipped with the repo.
- **COMPANY** — customer documents ingested via the `/documents` endpoint. Curated uploads only — synced Notion pages do not land here.
- **NOTION_WIKI** — optional Notion sync (`NOTION_SYNC_ENABLED`) incrementally re-indexes pages shared with a Notion internal integration into a separate `notion_wiki` collection (`type=notion`). A Notion share is inherited and multi-writer, so this text is unreviewed relative to curated company docs; the retriever labels it as such and ranks it below COMPANY. Un-shared pages are purged on the next tick.
- **FAILURES** — recorded failure cases (queried by `retrieve_failures`) teaching specialists what to avoid.
- **RECENT_RESEARCH** — web-research artifacts persisted from `executive_research` runs, kept separate from COMPANY so unvetted machine-generated text never blends into curated knowledge, and ranked below company documents.

A sixth collection, **SKILLS** (`openexecutive.knowledge.skills_index`), lives in the same `ChromaDBStore` and holds one document per skill (no chunking; the search corpus is `name` + `description` + `when_to_use`). It's reachable two ways:

1. **On demand, Executive-only** — the model explicitly calls the `search_skills` tool, then `load_skill` to fetch the full body, the same pattern as `web_search`. This is how the Executive finds and reuses its own repeatable task templates (a board memo, a quarterly forecast) when a user's own request resembles work it's codified before.
2. **Automatic, per-specialist, domain-gated** — `retriever.retrieve_skills()` (added alongside `retrieve()`/`retrieve_failures()` in `route_parallel`'s per-call fan-out) auto-injects at most one matched skill into a specialist's own context during a consult, but only when `skills_index.skills_active_for()` confirms that specialist's `BaseAgent.domain` has any populated skill content — a plain existence check, no cache, since it's a local embedded-Chroma lookup (sub-2ms). Deliberately keyed off `agent.domain`, NOT `DOMAIN_ALIASES` below — those two mappings disagree for several specialists (`grc`'s alias list is `["governance", "compliance"]` and never contains `"security"`, even though `GRCAgent.domain == "security"`, which is where its skill content actually lives). Today only `category: security` is populated with consult-style content, so this path is live for `ciso`/`cyberops`/`grc` and inert for every other specialist until someone authors skill content in their domain. A hit's body goes through the same `_format_untrusted_wiki` untrusted-content treatment as synced Notion text when `source == "company"` (a company-authored skill can be created by a prompt-injected Executive and later replayed into a *different* specialist's context); `source == "builtin"` skills are shipped with the repo and stay at BUILTIN's trust tier. When this path is active for a specialist, that specialist's own `n_builtin` drops by one (floored at 1) to keep the combined per-consult context budget close to prior levels rather than additive on top of it.

Each parallel specialist call runs its own domain-filtered query. When no explicit filter is passed, `DOMAIN_ALIASES` maps the specialist key to its domains — e.g. `cso`→`strategy`, `cpo`→`product`,`strategy`, `board_comms`→`board`,`finance`. Hits beyond a cosine distance threshold are dropped, and very short messages (greetings) bypass retrieval entirely.

Multi-domain chunks fan out to one row per declared domain, so `_dedupe_by_text` drops duplicate-text hits while preserving relevance order before results are returned.

The formatted context is injected into the **user turn** (wrapped in `<relevant_knowledge>` by `BaseAgent.analyze`), never into a cached system block — per-query hits would otherwise poison the prompt cache.
